note: size drifts on a days timescale but the only stale-size channel is bounded at 300s, so it is arithmetically negligible; the residual question (do losses land at above-average size) is n=12 closes with an MDE far above any plausible effect -- no power, and a restatement of the record either way
a disk stop ends the tape exogenously to market state, so it is missing-at-random w.r.t. the population question; R05 is a population-DEFINITION problem that no amount of complete tape fixes

B03 is a bound derived from arithmetic (MAX_PER_CLOSE x size x ceiling) and holds for any population; a rate fact has nothing to say about a maximum, and the only version that would connect them is a forbidden loss-rate-from-tape estimate

both are silent-failure modes, but pairing them yields only an ops health monitor, not a measurement; the targeted version that IS worth running is the F-I10 x F-M08 lead, and proposing the general 376-hour census alongside it would cost a day for the same answer

F-O07's 'the other side did not change' (88.6 -> 86.8%) was never clustered by close and never had an MDE stated -- if the design effect applies it may be no-power, not no-effect, and that claim is load-bearing for 'what changed is the MODEL'

the low-volatility worst-arm finding rests on 8 closes; a 300s collector gap leaves partial index coverage that both depresses measured sigma and corrupts locked_sum, so check index-print completeness on those 8 closes before spending a day on the clustered test
already measured both ways: the 250ms forward gap IS 3.18pp and the clean backward version has MDE 4.05pp with no power (F-R06). Nothing new to compute.

F-X04 is an API encoding convention, not a population. Any link runs through 'does the contest code count both sides symmetrically', which is a code audit, not a measurement, and I cannot name an artefact for it.

latency is already shown irrelevant to fills (F-P04, 96ms both). The only untried version -- latency of orders that LOST -- rests on ~10 losing closes against a 96/116ms distribution: no power, and no mechanism, since F-X03 means we fill at the resting price regardless.
you cannot calibrate a model on series that have never run a market. Zero rows. Contradiction 3 is closed.

both rules are already applied at their conservative limit -- we cluster by close time, which assumes 1 observation per close, and F-B03 bounds the worst close by construction. Measuring our own intra-close loss correlation rests on 10 losing closes: cannot separate rho 0.6 from 0.9.
coin identity failed as a risk sorter; sweep intensity in the 60s BEFORE the signal is a per-event sorter we already hold and have never scored.
collector gaps are hour-sized, not 5-min (F-I05); count index coverage per close and check the unexplained 1.87->4.61pp deterioration is not a tape artefact
a level-clearing sweep fills every resting order regardless of queue position, so the swept-volume fraction is a queue-free LOWER BOUND on maker fill rate -- no simulator needed
break-even 8.55% is a point estimate off 10 losing closes; put an interval on it before comparing to our loss rate
the refused dump-guard rows are a cross-coin jump marker; at rho 0.65 a refusal on one coin is news about the coins we do trade
chain strike(N+1)==settle(N) suggests bad closes cluster, but pinflood already tested it: prev_z 0.86x [0.55,1.36], prev_worst_any 0.93x, both flat, and F-P08 live agrees. Re-walking measured ground.
only link is 'both could be silently wrong' -- an analogy, not a mechanism. A fee reconciliation against actual billings is hygiene, not a measurement connecting these two.

inverting trade prices to an implied sd to test its tau-scaling is ill-conditioned exactly where we trade (F-C07: zero sigma sensitivity at 50c), and edge-by-tau is measurable directly per candidate without the inversion. Roundabout route to an answer already in reach.
dead series and post-loss behaviour share no mechanism. Nothing to compute.
volatility mix WITHIN coin is the one explanation of the 1.87->4.61 doubling not yet ruled out -- coin mix and drift are; decompose candidates by rv_short fifth, early edges applied late

scaling sd by k keeps the highest-z rows and z is high when sd is small, so k may have failed by COMPOSITION into the bad volatility fifth, not because the error is shape -- one cross-tab separates them
Edge size has a floor in the gate and no ceiling; bucket discount_c against model-wrong on the cached candidate rows, holding price and tau fixed.
Test whether quote age survives conditioning on time-since-index-print: a young quote may just be everyone repricing off the 1/sec tick we also see.

Cross-coin correlation from the shared 60s averaging window is just rho restated; already measured (0.62-0.69, design effect 31-46x) and already bounded by MAX_PER_CLOSE. No new number changes a decision.
Sweep leg counts are a worse instrument for hedge-side depth than the orderbook we already record directly; hedge decay was measured at five sizes and live hedge events are n=3.
Killed by arithmetic: the per-ORDER fee ceiling is 0.0001 dollars, so 362 live orders cap the rounding cost at 3.6 cents total, and fee is 0.3 percent of the worst-close bound.
Duplicate: CURRENT_STATE already flags the unchanged-counterparty claim as having no stated power, from an earlier collide run. Re-raising it adds a record, not a lead.

size has no variation independent of calendar time: it only moves when the bank moves (slow, monotone up) or after a loss (endogenous to the outcome), so a size-vs-fill-quality slope is collinear with the tape deterioration and with recent losses; no clean within-period contrast exists

the natural measurement -- set size from the measured 2.90% rather than the claimed 0.15% -- is forbidden: 2.90% is a TAPE-population rate and rule 5 bars using it for our exposure. The legal version (size from live loss rate + live loss sizes) already exists in pinbank

newseries.py and F-C10 already enumerate the silently-skipped tickers; counting distinct series in the cached candidate rows is a one-line sanity check, not a measurement, and no new number comes out of it

killed on power before it costs a day: splitting the 0.697pp offer/no-offer gap by tau band leaves ~140 effective rows per cell after the 31-46x design effect, on a 1-3% base -- MDE roughly 10x the effect. Subsumed by the F-M07 x F-R01 lead, which computes that interval once at the margin

the worst-close bound is a LOSS bound, but F-X04 makes the hedge a second PURCHASE, not a sale -- so cash committed on one close can reach entry+hedge while the sizer and MAX_RUN_STAKE were both derived from entry alone; measure whether our own stake rail can refuse the hedge at the worst moment

the 26x offer/no-offer selection gap (0.697pp absolute) has never had a close-time-clustered interval or an MDE printed; at a 31-46x design effect the effective failure count is single digits, so a load-bearing settled conclusion may rest on an unstated null
Does the market OFFER us our side more readily in the within-coin low-sigma fifth, where the model is 43.7x overconfident? F-P04 rules out latency, so a gap is the counterparty's choice.
Forced. Any hour-of-day question here runs on the model output and the outcome alone; taker_outcome_side contributes nothing to it, and the hour-of-day test exists independently of this pair.
Last-minute trade rate is BELOW uniform (5% vs 6.7%), so the last-minute book may be the earlier book: measure the age of resting asks at tau 60->3.
Decompose the 12.5x->28.2x overconfidence drift into a shift in the fresh/stale ask mix versus a within-age-bucket change; tau is the confound.
NO POWER, not no effect: 12 losing closes across 5 sigma fifths (expected 2.4 each) cannot separate 5.19% from 1.38%. The F-M08 x F-P04 lead is the powered version.
F-O07 checked contest, speed and depth but never ask AGE, so 'the counterparty did not change' is untested in the one dimension F-O06 names. Same measurement as F-M05 x F-O06 -- one job, not two.
300s size re-read divides the 900s window exactly and is blocked while in position -- measure whether we ever entered a close sized on a pre-settlement bank
no causal path (the live bot reads its own index socket, not the recorded tape) and the joint test is 12 losses against restart hours -- no power, and volatility confounds both

replacing a hard bound with an empirical concurrency is the exact mistake F-B03 is worded to prevent; and the candidate rows are the tape population, which cannot say how many would have been offered to US (F-R05, 31x)
one file per channel per HOUR covers all 12 series, so a truncated file is common-mode across coins and cannot manufacture a coin ranking; the only residual is reduced n, already the stated cause
76 of 283 live fills came in strictly BETTER than signalled -- measure whether price improvement is a stale quoter (a gift) or an informed one (adverse selection), by signed index markout in sd units
a zero-fill costs nothing but one loss undoes 27 wins, so if the 28.2%% that fill nothing are enriched in losers the miss rate is PROTECTIVE and raising it destroys money

Volume concentration and fill-price mechanics share no population. The only joint number (does price improvement vary by tau) has n=283 fills clustering to ~60 closes, and buys nothing: we already receive the resting price automatically, so no action follows from either answer.

Re-proposes exactly what F-R06 killed: reconstructing the adversely-selected population from the trade tape, no power, MDE 4.05pp. Any forward-looking version is poisoned by F-O05 -- taken-ness is partly CAUSED by the outcome, leak already 3.18pp at 250ms. A bigger-edge-taken-faster result is what leakage produces.

Sizing on stated confidence needs stated confidence to order the realised bad rate. Already measured that it does not: 19x wrong (F-M04), drifting 12.5x->28.2x (F-M05), and distrusting it more makes the rate WORSE (F-M06). F-B01's 300s flat-only refresh is orthogonal plumbing.

The tempting move -- use the 1/sec index to settle whether 248 closes are above break-even -- is illegal: our loss rate is not computable from the index, only the model-wrong rate is (F-R05). And that index-only rate is already pincalib's 2.90% (F-M04). Subsumed by the F-B06 x F-M07 lead, which uses the same population.

F-B06's back-to-back arithmetic assumes closes are independent; F-M07 names a sub-population where the model fails 26x. Measure lag-1 persistence of model error from the index alone -- but strike(N+1)==settle(N) means adjacent closes share data by construction.
A zero-fill close carries no position, so at a 28.2% zero-fill rate F-P08's 18-close denominator is nearer 13. Recompute it on closes that actually held contracts.
hedge fill price has never been checked against the quote it was sent into; F-X03's fill-quality evidence is all entry orders

the only bridge is 'does the adverse-selection gap vary by hour of day', and the gap is a loss rate for US: live fills only, ~248 closes split 24 ways is under 1.2 independent obs per bucket. No power at any n we will hold this year, and the underpowered version is exactly the one that gets run from the tape and breaks rule 5.

four series with zero settled markets have no book, no fills and no tape; there is no number to compute. The real open question about F-C10 (listed-but-unrecorded vs never listed) is an F-I07 question and does not use F-P10 at all.

the only measurement using both is dump-guard refusal rate by coin over the 16,683 rows. It is cheap, but it could only explain a NULL and P11 is a non-replication, which noise explains better; and the downstream question (is any coin safer for US) needs our loss rate, i.e. live fills, i.e. 248 closes over 12 coins. The table changes nothing.

same finding twice: R06 IS the attempt to bridge R05 and it was killed. Tempting because MDE 4.05pp sits just above the 3.3pp gap, so more tape looks like the fix -- it is not. MDE scales 1/sqrt(n) so 1.5x tape gives 3.3pp, i.e. 50% power, and more importantly the binding constraint is observability not power: the 82c XRP fill does not exist anywhere in the replayed book. More of an invisible thing is still invisible. Do not resurrect.

does the counterparty behave differently in the worst (lowest) volatility fifth -- full-level consumption rate at MATCHED resting depth, plus a stale-index control. Separates 'our sigma estimator breaks at low vol' from 'low vol attracts informed takers', which is the whole fix.

our size is set by the bank with no reference to depth, and the supply we face is one level taken whole. Measure available depth at the signal millisecond divided by our order size, over the bank's growth, to put a number on the capacity ceiling CURRENT_STATE #9 already identified.
